tagline: Accumulates a measure from the start of the fiscal or calendar year to the current date

slides.title: Year-to-Date Accumulation
slides.body: TOTALYTD calculates a measure by accumulating values from the start of the year through the latest date in the current filter context. Instead of seeing each month in isolation, users see a running total that grows through the year — essential for YTD Revenue, YTD Budget vs. Actual, and cumulative KPI tracking.
slides.keyPoint: TOTALYTD(measure, date_column) resets to zero on January 1 (or your fiscal year-start) and adds each period cumulatively. Requires a marked Date Table.

slides.title: Monthly Sales — Raw Data
slides.caption: Each month shows only that month's Sales — no accumulation yet
slides.note: The report is filtered to 2024. Without YTD logic, each month shows only its own sales.

slides.title: Defining the YTD Measure
slides.code:
Sales YTD =
TOTALYTD(
    [Total Sales],
    DimDate[Date]
)

-- Equivalent using CALCULATE + DATESYTD:
Sales YTD =
CALCULATE(
    [Total Sales],
    DATESYTD(DimDate[Date])
)
slides.annotation: TOTALYTD is shorthand for CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESYTD(DimDate[Date])). Both forms are equivalent and produce identical results. DATESYTD returns a table of all dates from Jan 1 to the last date in the current filter.

slides.title: Result — Running YTD Accumulation
slides.caption: Sales YTD accumulates from January 1, adding each month cumulatively

slides.title: Fiscal Year Support
bullets: Default year-end is December 31. For fiscal years that end on a different date, add the year-end-date parameter.
Fiscal year ending June 30: TOTALYTD([Total Sales], DimDate[Date], "06/30")
Fiscal year ending March 31: TOTALYTD([Total Sales], DimDate[Date], "03/31")
The year-end date tells TOTALYTD when to reset the accumulation to zero and start a new YTD cycle
slides.keyPoint: The optional third argument to TOTALYTD is the fiscal year-end date in MM/DD format. Without it, December 31 is assumed.
slides.warning: Without the fiscal year-end parameter, a company with a July–June fiscal year will see incorrect YTD values — the accumulation resets at the wrong time.

slides.title: Prerequisites and Common Mistakes
bullets: DimDate must be marked as a Date Table (Table Tools → Mark as Date Table) — otherwise TOTALYTD returns BLANK
DimDate must have a contiguous date range with no gaps — missing dates cause incorrect YTD accumulation
TOTALYTD resets at the fiscal year-start — do not confuse with TOTALQTD (quarter-to-date) or TOTALMTD (month-to-date)
If the Date column passed to TOTALYTD is not from the marked Date Table, time intelligence will not work correctly
slides.warning: If TOTALYTD returns BLANK or the same value as the monthly measure, the most likely cause is: (1) the Date table is not marked as Date Table, or (2) the DimDate[Date] column passed has date gaps. Check the Date Table settings first.

slides.title: TOTALYTD vs DATESYTD — Exam Clarity
bullets: TOTALYTD(measure, date) — a self-contained time intelligence function. Takes a measure directly.
DATESYTD(date) — returns a table of dates from year-start to the current date. Used inside CALCULATE.
CALCULATE([Total Sales], DATESYTD(DimDate[Date])) is identical to TOTALYTD([Total Sales], DimDate[Date])
DATESYTD gives more flexibility: you can add additional CALCULATE filters alongside it
PL-300 tests both forms — know that TOTALYTD is shorthand for the CALCULATE + DATESYTD pattern
slides.keyPoint: Choose TOTALYTD for concise YTD measures. Choose CALCULATE + DATESYTD when you need additional filter conditions beyond the YTD date range.
